content: {"summary":"The NXDOMAIN responses on orders‑api in March 2025 were caused by a zone push to internal‑dns‑01 that omitted the database record used by orders‑api. CoreDNS cached the missing record on the server that received the new file, while the other DNS server still served the correct record, leading to intermittent failures. The issue was resolved by re‑adding the missing record, pushing an updated zone file to internal‑dns‑01 at 15:38, and allowing the cache to expire, after which all lookups succeeded.","likely_cause":"Missing DNS record in the zone file deployed to internal‑dns‑01 during the 15:15 March 2025 push","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The new zone file lacked the record orders‑api uses for its database, causing NXDOMAIN lookups.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#0"],"quote":"The new file lacked the record orders-api uses for its database."},{"text":"Only internal‑dns‑01 served the new file, so CoreDNS cache sometimes returned NXDOMAIN and sometimes the correct address, causing intermittent failures.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#1"],"quote":"Only internal-dns-01 served the new file, so a cache period ... came back NXDOMAIN and one ... came back with the address."},{"text":"The missing record was re‑added, a corrected zone file was pushed to internal‑dns‑01 at 15:38, and after the cache turned over lookups succeeded consistently.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#2","INC-0025#3"],"quote":"The record went back into the zone source ... corrected file went out ... at 15:38"}],"next_checks":["Verify the current prod.internal zone on both internal‑dns‑01 and internal‑dns‑02 contains the required database record","Monitor CoreDNS cache TTL to ensure stale negative responses are cleared promptly","Implement post‑push validation that critical records resolve correctly on all DNS servers"]}
